Original SQL - 21/08/24

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.views_nearest_posts AS SELECT posts.id, posts.category_id, posts.created_at, posts.animation, posts.animation_filter, posts.description, posts.slug, posts.little_planet, posts.little_planet_filter, posts.location_post, posts.location_name, posts.panorama, posts.thumbnail, posts.panorama_preview, posts.post_type, posts.panorama_quality, posts.pending, posts.user_id, posts.location_post->>'latitude' AS latitude, posts.location_post->>'longitude' AS longitude, users.avatar, users.fullname, users.username, users.encrypt, CASE WHEN broadcast.post_id IS NOT NULL THEN true ELSE false END AS potd, CASE WHEN broadcast.post_id IS NOT NULL THEN json_build_object('title', broadcast.title, 'message', broadcast.messages) ELSE NULL END AS broadcast_data, jsonb_build_object('avatar', users.avatar, 'fullname', users.fullname, 'username', users.username, 'user_id', users.id) AS data_user, posts.hide, posts.score_timeline, posts.score_updated_at, posts.panorama_web, COALESCE(json_agg(DISTINCT json_build_object('filter', lp.filter_value, 'filter_type', lp.filter_type)) FILTER (WHERE lp.filter_value IS NOT NULL), '[]'::JSONB) AS little_planet_filters, COALESCE(json_agg(DISTINCT json_build_object('animation_value', ap.animation_value)) FILTER (WHERE ap.animation_value IS NOT NULL), '[]') AS animation_posts FROM panorra_dev.public.posts LEFT JOIN panorra_dev.public.users ON users.id = posts.user_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT ON (post_id) post_id, title, messages FROM panorra_dev.public.broadcast ORDER BY post_id, created_at DESC) AS broadcast ON broadcast.post_id = posts.id LEFT JOIN panorra_dev.public.little_planet_filter AS lp ON lp.post_id = posts.id LEFT JOIN panorra_dev.public.animation_post AS ap ON ap.post_id = posts.id WHERE (((((posts.is_publish = true) AND (posts.location_name IS NOT NULL)) AND ((posts.location_post->>'latitude') IS NOT NULL)) AND ((posts.location_post->>'latitude') != '')) AND ((posts.location_post->>'longitude') IS NOT NULL)) AND ((posts.location_post->>'longitude') != '') GROUP BY posts.id, posts.category_id, posts.created_at, posts.animation, posts.animation_filter, posts.description, posts.slug, posts.little_planet, posts.little_planet_filter, posts.location_post, posts.location_name, posts.panorama, posts.thumbnail, posts.panorama_preview, posts.post_type, posts.panorama_quality, posts.pending, posts.user_id, users.avatar, users.fullname, users.username, users.encrypt, users.id, broadcast.post_id, broadcast.messages, broadcast.title, posts.hide, posts.score_timeline, posts.score_updated_at, posts.panorama_web;

QA Summary - 5 August 2026

Verdict: PASSED. The active developer contract for views_nearest_posts requires published public posts with a location and latitude/longitude, and excludes banned posts and posts owned by banned users. Real Dev read requests confirm the observable visibility rule: across the tester's complete 199-post timeline, all 17 private and 10 unlisted records were absent from the nearest-post response, while 98 public tester records were present. The nearest response returned 851 records, every returned record had latitude and longitude, and no HTTP 500 occurred on the valid route.

QA Summary - 5 August 2026

Verdict: PASSED. The latest developer update requires views_blocked_posts to expose only public, non-banned posts from non-banned owners. Real Dev testing used only the approved tester accounts: tester account A blocked one existing public post owned by tester account B, verified it appeared in the blocked-post list, then immediately unblocked it and verified the list was empty again. The target row was exposed only while the block existed; no HTTP 500 occurred on the valid task APIs.

COALESCE(json_agg(DISTINCT json_build_object('comment_slug', l_nodes.comment_slug, 'user', json_build_object('username', l_users.username, 'fullname', l_users.fullname))) FILTER (WHERE l_nodes.user_id IS NOT NULL), '[]') AS like_comments
FROM panorra_dev.public.comment AS c
LEFT JOIN panorra_dev.public.users ON users.id = c.user_id
LEFT JOIN panorra_dev.public.posts AS p ON c.post_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT comment_id, count(*) AS likes_count FROM panorra_dev.public.like_comment GROUP BY comment_id) AS l ON l.comment_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN panorra_dev.public.like_comment AS l_nodes ON l_nodes.comment_id = c.id LEFT JOIN panorra_dev.public.users AS l_users ON l_users.id = l_nodes.user_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.parent_id, c.comment_value, c.created_at, users.avatar, users.fullname, users.username, users.country, l.likes_count, p.slug, c.slug, p.id, users.encrypt;
